_note: Labelled probe set for offline evaluation of the layer-3 narrative reader against LCD L34220 criterion C2. Each probe carries a structured label: whether findable support exists, where it sits, and — for hard negatives — why the plausible-looking evidence does not count. The harness (scripts/evaluate.py) scores any outputs file against these labels.
_provenance: Probe documents are synthetic and written to exercise one named failure class each. Clinical phrasing follows the conventions of real therapy discharge summaries and office notes; no real record, member or provider is reproduced. Labels are authored, not adjudicated — a production gold set would be physician-adjudicated with two independent reviewers and a tracked inter-rater agreement rate. That number is the ceiling on achievable performance and is currently UNMEASURED here.
_samplingWarning: This is a CONSTRUCTED adversarial slice, not a random sample. Hard negatives are over-represented on purpose, because Cheng-class failures are rare in a random draw and catastrophic for reviewer trust. Precision and recall computed on this slice are diagnostic, not prevalence estimates. Never pool these with the random-sample queue metrics.

sections.heading: ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

sections.heading: TREATMENT LOG

sections.heading: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
sections.text: Patient completed a six-week course of skilled physical therapy directed at the lumbar spine. Pain and functional limitation are essentially unchanged from intake. label.notes: Lumbar-directed, six weeks, explicit non-response. Unambiguous positive.

probes.description: Cheng class. A complete, well-formatted therapy record that exceeds four weeks — treating a different body region. The record is authentic and the citation will verify; it is simply not about this complaint.

claimsLayer.basis: 18 paid therapy claims 2026-02-10 to 2026-04-07, every claim carrying diagnosis pointer M75.101 (rotator cuff tear, right shoulder). No lumbar-directed conservative management appears in claims.

sections.heading: HISTORY
sections.text: Low back pain for several months. Patient reports extensive physical therapy this year. Requesting lumbar MRI.

sections.heading: EPISODE OF CARE
sections.text: Treating Diagnosis: Rotator cuff tear, right shoulder (M75.101). Dates of Service: 02/10/2026 through 04/07/2026. Eighteen visits completed.

sections.heading: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
sections.text: Patient completed an eight-week course of skilled physical therapy without meaningful improvement in pain or function. Symptoms have not responded to conservative management including therapeutic exercise, manual therapy, and an independent home exercise program. GOALS: 0 of 3 functional goals met. Postural screening performed at intake noted mild lumbar discomfort with prolonged sitting; not addressed in this episode.

label.whyNot: The therapy episode treated a right shoulder rotator cuff tear. The quoted non-response language is authentic and will pass citation verification, but it describes shoulder-directed care. The only lumbar mention is incidental postural screening explicitly not addressed in the episode. Conservative management for the lumbar complaint did not occur.
label.catchableBy: Body-region consistency: request region (lumbar, M54.50) does not match evidence region (shoulder, M75.101).

probes.description: Everything matches except the half that matters. Lumbar-directed, recent, well past four weeks — and the patient got better. Tests whether the reader checks the non-response half of the criterion or stops at duration.

claimsLayer.basis: 10 paid therapy claims 2026-05-04 to 2026-06-19, CPT 97110, lumbar diagnosis pointer M51.36

sections.heading: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
sections.text: Treating Diagnosis: Lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration (M51.36). Dates of Service: 05/04/2026 through 06/19/2026. Patient completed a seven-week course of skilled physical therapy directed at the lumbar spine. GOALS: 4 of 4 functional goals met. Pain reduced from 7/10 at intake to 2/10 at discharge. Patient returned to full work duties without restriction and was discharged to an independent home exercise program.

sections.heading: ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
sections.text: Known lumbar degenerative disc disease, clinically stable. Patient completed physical therapy earlier this year. Requesting MRI for further characterisation of known findings. No new neurological symptoms. No surgical consultation pending.

label.whyNot: A four-week trial demonstrably occurred, so the duration half of C2 is satisfied — but the criterion requires that the patient HAS NOT responded. Goals were fully met and pain dropped from 7/10 to 2/10. Reporting this as support for C2 inverts the criterion.
label.catchableBy: Narrative only. Claims confirm duration and cannot see outcome — this is precisely the half the claims ledger cannot answer.

probes.description: Future tense. All the right vocabulary, none of it having happened yet. Tests tense and modality handling.

claimsLayer.basis: No paid conservative management claims in the 18-month lookback.

sections.heading: ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
sections.text: Low back pain, onset approximately three weeks ago. Plan: the patient will begin a six-week course of skilled physical therapy focused on lumbar stabilisation and therapeutic exercise, starting the week of 09/14/2026. We anticipate that symptoms will not respond to conservative management given the severity at presentation, and I am requesting lumbar MRI now so that imaging is available if therapy fails.

label.whyNot: The therapy is prospective. 'Will begin', 'starting the week of', and 'we anticipate' describe a plan, not a completed trial. The criterion requires a trial that has occurred and to which the patient has not responded. Onset three weeks ago also makes a completed four-week trial impossible.
label.catchableBy: Partially — claims show zero conservative management, so the claims layer contradicts any narrative finding of a completed trial.

probes.description: Contains every keyword the reader is looking for, inside a negation. The classic extraction trap.

claimsLayer.basis: No paid conservative management claims in the 18-month lookback.

sections.heading: ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
sections.text: Discussed a four-week trial of conservative management including physical therapy, therapeutic exercise and anti-inflammatory medication. The patient declined physical therapy, citing work schedule and prior dissatisfaction with therapy for an unrelated condition. No course of conservative management was undertaken. Proceeding directly to a request for lumbar MRI at the patient's preference.

label.whyNot: The passage discusses conservative management in order to record that it did not happen. 'The patient declined' and 'no course of conservative management was undertaken' negate the very thing the criterion requires. Quoting the first sentence alone would pass citation verification and invert the meaning.
label.catchableBy: Partially — claims show zero conservative management, contradicting any positive narrative finding.

probes.description: Real, lumbar-directed, non-responsive — and two weeks long. Tests whether the stated duration bar is actually enforced.

claimsLayer.basis: 4 paid therapy claims 2026-08-04 to 2026-08-17, lumbar diagnosis pointer M54.50. Span is 13 days — under the four-week threshold.

sections.heading: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
sections.text: Treating Diagnosis: Low back pain (M54.50). Dates of Service: 08/04/2026 through 08/17/2026. Four visits completed. Patient discontinued therapy early citing lack of benefit. Symptoms have not responded to conservative management to date. GOALS: 0 of 3 functional goals met.

label.whyNot: Lumbar-directed and genuinely non-responsive, but the episode spans 13 days against a criterion that requires at least four weeks. The non-response language is real and will verify; the trial is simply too short to satisfy C2.
label.catchableBy: Claims span arithmetic: 2026-08-04 to 2026-08-17 is 13 days, under the 28-day threshold.
